source.title: A simple connection from loss flatness to compressed neural representations
source.authors: Shirui Chen; Stefano Recanatesi; Eric T. Shea-Brown

record.tranche_reason: The study measures sharpness-related quantities alongside the generalization gap, using correlation analyses rather than the magnitude-aware perturbation ranking specified in V7.
record.gate_note: Results about how sharpness and representation-compression metrics relate to each other do not bear on the listed versions unless they also measure the generalization gap. The paper discusses several prior studies, but those cited results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures Hessian-trace sharpness and last-layer relative flatness against generalization gaps, but neither measures V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance before training error rises. Its elementwise-adaptive perturbation experiment measures representation sensitivity rather than generalization. These findings do not test the specifically stated V7, and the batch-size experiments do not establish V5's fixed-epoch comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors establish upper bounds linking sharpness-related quantities to local representation compression and report stronger empirical associations with compression than with generalization. They explicitly state that lower sharpness need not imply better test accuracy. The bounds also depend on weight and input factors, so sharpness alone does not unconditionally determine compression.
record.recipe_differences: Measures correlations between sharpness-related metrics, representation-compression measures, and generalization gap; does not apply the magnitude-aware sharpness comparison in V7.
record.method_sensitivity: The relationship depends on the sharpness and compression measure: single-layer MLS bounds and relative flatness can correlate negatively or weakly, while NMLS bounds correlate positively with NMLS. For pretrained ViTs, unnormalized metrics do not show the reported correlation; normalized MLS and elementwise-adaptive sharpness do.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 100 models per architecture/dataset setting, Hessian-trace sharpness correlates positively with the generalization gap, whereas last-layer relative flatness has weak or sometimes negative correlation (Section H.2, Figures H.7–H.9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The association between curvature-based sharpness and generalization gaps depends on the sharpness measure and model setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 181 pretrained ViTs, elementwise-adaptive sharpness generally correlates positively with normalized maximum local sensitivity, with outlier model families; the corresponding unnormalized metrics do not show this correlation (Section 4.3, Figure 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-scaled sharpness can track local representation sensitivity across pretrained vision transformers.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report that sharpness correlates more consistently with compression metrics than with generalization gaps, and that lower sharpness does not always accompany better test accuracy (Section 5 and Appendix I).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Lower Hessian-trace sharpness does not universally imply higher held-out accuracy.

record.problems: Generalization-gap findings are presented as correlation analyses; exact coefficients appear in figures, and the study reports that sharpness is more strongly correlated with compression metrics than with the generalization gap. The paper notes that weight-related prefactors can vary across configurations.
record.rows_left_out: No rows extracted. The study's relevant generalization-gap findings are stated in text and shown in correlation plots, but they do not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness or its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy comparison.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects at equal epoch budgets and adaptations that remove those effects; the supplied trajectories use iteration counts.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and removal of dropout with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus training–test error gaps, including its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. The generalization analyses use different sharpness measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record's classification of V7 as tested is too broad for the supplied version. Reparametrization invariance alone does not make last-layer relative flatness equivalent to V7's perturbation-tolerance measure. Generalization-gap results are already declared in rows_left_out and do not warrant missing entries for V7. No result rows were supplied.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers and held-out performance.
Large-batch versus small-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.

Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures are not tested. The study reports correlations for standard sharpness and relative flatness against the generalization gap, but the numerical figure values are not extracted as distinct rows.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Sections 5 and H.2 discuss sharpness and generalization using Hessian-trace sharpness and last-layer relative flatness; neither directly tests V7's specified measure and comparison.

tranche.reason: The study measures related constructs rather than V7's magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance before training error rises. Its adaptive-sharpness experiment concerns representation sensitivity, not generalization-gap ranking.

source_check.notes: Section H.2 reports positive sharpness–gap correlations but weak or negative last-layer relative-flatness correlations. These concern different measures from V7 and do not warrant a verdict on that version.
